original_test_intent: Verify that Type 17 Speed reports the approved maximum capable transfer rate for each memory device in MT/s, uses the correct legacy/Extended Speed representation, remains distinct from the configured operating rate, and is semantically stable after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw Type 17 records and SMBIOS version; bind Speed, Extended Speed and Configured Memory Speed to locator/module identity, apply versioned unknown/selector rules and structure-length checks, normalize MT/s, compare trusted module capability and configured relationship, then repeat after reboot.
manual_activity: A user approves module capability/operating-speed policy and reboot plan. No clock change or stress execution is part of this metadata case.
required_inputs: Expected maximum capable Speed per device/locator
Applicable SMBIOS version, structure length and Speed/Extended Speed rules
Expected Configured Memory Speed relationship and permitted down-clocking
Raw-capable parser and approved reboot/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS and approved inventory; do not change memory frequency, timings or firmware.
Anchor each speed field by exact offset/name; do not accept a generic grep mixture.
Apply versioned unknown/extended selector semantics and gate extension fields by structure length.
Keep capable Speed, configured operating speed and clock-frequency terminology distinct; report units as MT/s.
Stop on illegal field relationship, identity ambiguity or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Decode per-device raw legacy/extended capable speed, compare approved module capability and configured-rate relationship, then compare pre/post reboot semantics.
Do not alter frequency, benchmark memory or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve capable/configured speed baselines, down-clock policy and versioned field interpretation.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The word Speed is relevant but grep -iA1 matches multiple distinct fields, loses record identity and cannot prove legacy/extended selector or units.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 17 data; report locator/module identity, raw Speed, selector/unknown decision, raw Extended Speed, normalized capable MT/s and Configured Memory Speed separately.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The capable Speed scope, Type 17 script and 5/5-minute values are retained; log clearing and any frequency/hardware change are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Parse exact raw speed fields per Type 17 identity, apply SMBIOS version/length/selector rules, compare maximum module capability and configured operating rate under approved policy, and repeat after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 17 records including memory rates beyond the legacy Speed field range.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS/BMC, dmidecode/parser and optional SPD-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 17 Speed, Extended Speed and Configured Memory Speed definitions plus authoritative module/platform speed policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact-field identity, capable/configured separation, extension gating and MT/s normalization.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong-field matches, illegal selector/extension combinations, capability/configuration conflation and wrong-slot module speeds.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Per-device capability and configured-rate policy plus versioned field rules.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SMBIOS speed metadata does not prove runtime signal integrity, stability or benchmark bandwidth.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a configured speed below module capability due to CPU, topology or qualification limits, but must record both expected values; down-clocking is not automatically a failure and capable Speed must not be overwritten with configured rate.
expected_evidence: Approved platform/module identity, capable/configured speed baselines and SMBIOS version/selector policy
Per-device raw legacy/extended fields, selector decision and normalized capable MT/s
Configured Memory Speed and trusted module/SPD comparison kept as separate evidence
Approved reboot/health evidence and post-reboot semantic speed diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item targets the capable Speed field; related configured/extended fields clarify representation and do not conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact speed-field decoding and policy comparison are fully automatable after approved baselines.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects ambiguous broad matching and adds record identity, extended selector and capable/configured separation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains version-aware safety and module correlation while restoring FULLY AUTOMATABLE classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates metadata capability from runtime qualification and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents Configured Memory Speed or another grep match from being mistaken for module capability and detects invalid legacy/extended encodings.
independent_technical_reasoning: Speed fields are structured numeric metadata with deterministic selector and comparison rules; project limits and reboot approval affect readiness, not capability.
